statements.text: Our veterans deserve, and need, access to better healthcare services and our scientists should remain on the cutting edge of big data analytics and machine learning. The DOE and VA should be able to work together to improve the medical care of our veterans, who have sacrificed so much for our nation.
statements.venue: Press release on NDAA amendment for AI and high-performance computing research for veterans' health

statements.text: AI is a good thing and it’s a bad thing. It’s got the potential to do a lot of damage. It’s the coming wave of technology that every state will have to address. Congress will have to put guardrails in place. We can’t let it derail the country, and it has the potential to do that.
statements.venue: Washington Reporter interview on federal moratorium on state AI regulation

statements.text: Absolutely, it's too powerful. Anybody who has grandchildren, when what you see on TV and the dangers that it has, when they can make images exactly and imitate your voice. [...] It doesn't mean you stop trying. But yeah, you try to regulate what you can and find out what you can so that it's used in a good way instead of hurting American children and Americans in general.
statements.venue: SC GOP U.S. Senate runoff debate (C-SPAN transcript)

statements.text: I believe in the 10th Amendment state's rights. I think that for that data center that's being built, where it causes diminished value of homes around it, the community is going to have to take ownership and use what they can and find out what's the water usage do for their community. [...] The big thing I will do is not let the politicians in local communities or advocate for them not to give the farm away and not to have incentives for these data companies. Let them pay their own way.
statements.venue: SC GOP U.S. Senate runoff debate (C-SPAN transcript), on AI data centers

statements.text: Look, the way you have quality growth in South Carolina, and we've got a lot of people moving in, you empower the tech schools. The young people don't realize the opportunities there for that carpenter, that electrician, that person that uses his hands.
statements.venue: SC GOP U.S. Senate runoff debate (C-SPAN transcript), answer to question on AI and jobs

statements.text: It's too complex a subject. You've got to understand it.
